key_insight: PathMem introduces a cognition-aligned memory transformation that lets pathology MLLMs explicitly encode and retrieve structured domain knowledge (taxonomy, grading criteria, clinical evidence) to link visual findings with formal diagnostic rules in an interpretable way.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between raw visual recognition and structured diagnostic reasoning in computational pathology by providing an explicit, interpretable memory mechanism for integrating domain knowledge with multimodal features.
method: Cognition-aligned memory module: transform multimodal visual features into structured memory items that map to pathology taxonomy, grading criteria, and evidence tokens.
Interpretable memory access: explicit read/write and retrieval routines that support traceable linking between morphological evidence and formal diagnostic rules during reasoning.
Task-aligned training and prompts: supervise memory formation and retrieval with diagnostic/grading tasks so the MLLM learns to use the structured memory for decision-making and explanations.
impact: Enables more reliable, transparent diagnostic reasoning in pathology MLLMs by combining visual pattern recognition with explicit, interpretable domain knowledge—useful for clinical AI workflows, auditability, and downstream fine-tuning.
visual_elements: Schematic of PathMem architecture: image encoder → memory transformation layer → structured memory bank → MLLM reasoning loop
Example case flow: histology patch → extracted features → memory node activation → graded diagnosis with evidence links
Before/after comparison: standard MLLM output vs. PathMem-enhanced output showing improved interpretability and explicit references to criteria
Icon set: taxonomy tree, grading scale, evidence document, and memory cell to visually map concepts
paper_title: PathMem: Toward Cognition-Aligned Memory Transformation for Pathology MLLMs
paper_authors: Jinyue Li, Yuci Liang, Qiankun Li, Xinheng Lyu, Jiayu Qian
